headline: Stocks opened higher after a slightly cooler-than-expected October PPI, then gave it back as the chip trade that followed Huang's exit unwound: AMD -8.8%, AVGO -4.8%, SMH -3%, and NVDA swung from +2% to -2%. Money moved into staples, financials, energy and Meta, while Bitcoin broke below $70k on hawkish-Fed and dollar pressure.

Two things moved markets: Nvidia gapped down 13% after Jensen Huang resigned and buyers recovered most of it, then a Treasury selloff took the 10-year to 5.10%, worsened midday by Trump's Iran remarks and the oil jump that followed. That pushed gold, bitcoin and small caps lower while the S&P barely moved.

Chips led the market higher after CoreWeave's results revived the AI trade. Semis (SMH +4.8%) and the Nasdaq (+2.3%) gained mostly in the opening gap. Rates went nowhere after Tuesday's hot-CPI shock, while the dollar kept climbing on Fed hike bets.

Hotter-than-expected October CPI (headline +0.4%, core +0.3%, which meets Waller's stated bar for considering a 50bp hike) sent the 10-year yield back to about 5% (+12bp) and lifted the dollar while gold and TIPS fell. Stocks gapped lower but recovered most of the gap during the session. The day's real equity damage was concentrated in Nvidia (−5.5% on 3x volume, Huang scandal) and Microsoft (−2.2%, Anthropic Office-style tools).

Stocks had their best day since April 8 (S&P +2.35%, Dow +1,104) as last week's AI and semiconductor selloff reversed and oil fell about 4–6% on reports of a preliminary Iran deal. Nvidia was the exception, down 4.3% after its board opened a probe into Jensen Huang's alleged Chinese spy link.

Thursday's record chip rout (Nasdaq 100 −6.4%) partly reversed: chips and the Nasdaq gapped sharply higher and the dollar jumped on a blowout payrolls report (+165k vs ~59k expected), but much of the tech gap faded and defensives were sold, so the S&P only gained 0.3%.

A blue-wave backlash against the AI build-out erased Wednesday's post-midterm rally: semis lost 11.6%, the S&P 500 fell 4.4% (its worst day since April 2025) and the VIX jumped 70% to about 28. Bonds caught a modest bid and the dollar and gold barely moved.
